A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniFall benchmark. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, supervised and unsupervised segmentation, domain-distance, and demographic-transfer results in Section 4 and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds zero-shot MLLM comparisons, prompt ablations, and an experiment incorporating in-the-wild training data.

M1.justification: No substantive change to the proposed benchmark-construction method is established. Wan2.2 generation and the 16-class annotation scheme remain; expression conditioning and separate fallen-state examples already appear in v2's appendix. Added MLLMs are comparison baselines, while expanded annotation rules and removed classifier descriptions change documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight staged datasets, 818 in-the-wild videos, and 12,000 synthetic videos, with the same classification and timeline-segmentation tasks. New model comparisons and in-the-wild training use existing coverage. The pooled Fall/Fallen score changes evaluation reporting rather than introducing new data or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 introduces Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 zero-shot comparisons, including 2B, 4B, and 8B variants, plus Keye-VL-1.5-8B in Appendix A.7. Conversely, ASQuery with I3D features disappears from the segmentation comparison, leaving SigLIP2 results. TW-FINCH and KMeans are retained in the appendix, not removed.

E3.justification: v3 adds individual-dataset training comparisons, a combined staged/synthetic/wild training configuration, and pooled Fall-or-Fallen evaluation. New MLLM experiments introduce 16-frame, 448-pixel-square inputs and model-size and prompt-selection protocols, including selection informed by OF-ItW ablations. Existing CS/CV and demographic split definitions remain substantially unchanged; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds model-scale tests, detailed prompt-format/component/location ablations, and fallen-versus-lying confusion analysis (Figure 7 and Tables 7–10). It removes v2's temporal-trajectory and episode-completeness analysis, eight-class radar analysis, and I3D-versus-SigLIP2 segmentation comparison. Cross-age and cross-BMI tests are retained and moved to the appendix.

E5.justification: Appendix A.7 newly specifies inference seed 0 and fixed-seed temporal sampling for MLLM evaluation. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This is added seed disclosure, not evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: v3 Table 4 adds OF-ItW Fall/Fallen F1 scores of 67.8/29.2 for Qwen3-VL-8B and 68.0/31.0 for InternVL3.5-8B. The newly wild-trained VMAE configuration reports 76.0/53.6 under different training conditions. Extensive prompt, scale, and per-dataset results are added, while I3D segmentation, temporal-chain, and some CV-to-wild/synthetic entries disappear. Retained VMAE classification and SigLIP2 segmentation scores largely match v2.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. v3's class definitions clarify the existing annotation taxonomy; its pooled detection reporting is an evaluation addition rather than a mathematical extension.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes synthetic-versus-staged transfer and feature-dependent domain complementarity. v3 retains the benchmark contributions but makes the fine-tuned-versus-zero-shot fall/fallen distinction central in its abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It newly argues that fallen recognition requires task-specific training and identifies it as the principal clinical bottleneck, while dropping the earlier feature-dependent qualification of segmentation transfer.

C2.justification: v3 attributes synthetic training's fallen-state benefits to extended post-fall ground contact and interprets MLLM confusion through temporal reasoning, missed clinical alerts, and deployment cost. The earlier I3D-specific transfer explanation is removed. Limitations become more specific: OF-ItW overrepresents spectacular accidents relative to elderly-care falls, and synthetic generation has ethnicity-taxonomy and binary-gender constraints.

D1.justification: v3 adds precise class definitions, temporal-boundary conventions, and detailed MLLM prompts, preprocessing, decoding, and response parsing. It adds a direct dataset pointer and supplementary-browser instructions. Conversely, it removes v2's classifier optimizer and training-budget description, multi-view annotation-transfer procedure, deterministic generation-attribute assignment, and extraction-time estimate. The appendix still promises release upon acceptance, so the new access pointer does not establish availability.

R1.justification: The paper substantially expands its positioning from dataset unification and synthetic transfer to evaluating pretrained generalist MLLMs against smaller specialized models. Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Keye-VL, and vLLM/PagedAttention references support this new framing; an additional multi-camera fall-detection work is also cited. Much of the original dataset literature review remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset rationale, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v3 adds a main-text synthetic-data risks section and an appendix roadmap, reorganizes annotation and experimental documentation, and moves cross-view and demographic discussions into the appendix. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond added experiments alone.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout and rebuilds classification tables around test datasets, adding model rows, pooled detection columns, and OOD shading. It adds expression-conditioning and confusion figures plus definition and ablation tables, while removing radar, trajectory, and PRISMA-checklist displays. The demographic plot and twelve full-size embedding plots remain, with relocation and presentation edits.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful baselines, diagnostic ablations, an in-domain reference, and clearer annotation definitions. However, its new claim that fallen recognition requires task-specific training is not consistently supported: a zero-shot Qwen prompt variant reaches 45.4 Fallen F1 in Table 10, exceeding synthetic-trained VMAE's 42.3 in Table 4, with tradeoffs on other metrics. v3 also removes training details and v2's I3D results that qualified synthetic-data superiority. The expanded evidence improves usefulness, but unresolved central interpretations and lost documentation prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
